messages:
Jordan Li: Quick sync — I'm drafting a cross-team spec for audit event taxonomy + naming. Biggest constraints: (1) RBAC changes landing next week, (2) new KMS integration will add key-level events, (3) customers will validate audit streams against their own SIEM parsers. Need alignment on event names, fields, and what we guarantee back-compat for.

Sarah Chen: +1. can you list the required fields you think are immutable? that helps teams figure out mapping.

Jordan Li: Early proposal: immutable fields: `event_id`, `timestamp_iso8601`, `actor.type`, `actor.id`, `resource.type`, `resource.id`, `outcome` (enum: `success`|`failure`|`unknown`), `origin` (host/region). Everything else is extensible.

Mike Patel: That seems sane. Two questions: 1) do we namespace events by product area (e.g., `auth.user.login` vs `session.start`)? 2) KMS: will key operations include plaintext key material in any field (no!), and what about `key_version` vs `key_id`?

Jordan Li: Answer 1: prefer dotted namespace `service.object.action` e.g., `iam.user.grant_role`, `kms.key.rotate`. Helps filtering. Answer 2: No plaintext. For KMS, include `kms.key_id` (opaque), optional `kms.key_version` when rotation occurs, and `kms.operation` (create|rotate|delete|access).

Eva Gomez: + tagging on the dotted namespace. For customer-facing events we should also expose a "friendly" `event_name` string that maps to the formal event id for docs. That reduces confusion for SOCs.

Sarah Chen: Important: RBAC changes will add `actor.role_changes` events. We need to define what the `resource` is for role assign/unassign (user vs group). Suggest `resource.type = "rbac.assignment"` and include `payload.previous_roles` and `payload.new_roles`.

Jordan Li: Good call. I'll propose `rbac.assignment.create` / `rbac.assignment.delete` and include `payload` keys as you suggested. Keep payload schema optional but documented.

security-bot: FYI: vulnerability triage doc updated: CVE-2026-1021 affects token exchange flow; any event that logs tokens must be scrubbed.

Mike Patel: Noted. For audit schema, we should standardize `sensitive` flag on fields so downstream scrubbing is consistent. e.g., `fields_to_mask = ["auth.token","credentials.*"]` and `sensitive:true` metadata per field.

Jordan Li: Agree. Proposed mask approach: suppression at source for fields with `sensitive:true`, and `masking_policy` metadata at event-level (none|redact|hash). We'll make default `redact` for auth-related fields.

Eva Gomez: One more: customers will validate event streams. We should version the schema (v1,v2) in each event: `schema.version = "audit.v1"`. If we make non-breaking additions they stay same version; incompatible changes bump to `audit.v2`.

Jordan Li: Exactly. Plan to include `schema.version`, `event_id`, and `created_at` as immutable anchors. We'll publish a compatibility matrix in the docs.

Sarah Chen: Cross-team concern: Logs -> telemetry team wants `request_id` for traceability, infra wants `host` & `region`, product wants `feature_flag` context. Can we define a small core set and an `extensions` object for extras?

Jordan Li: Proposed core = [`event_id`,`timestamp_iso8601`,`actor.type`,`actor.id`,`resource.type`,`resource.id`,`outcome`,`schema.version`,`origin`]. Everything else goes into `context` (map string->any) and `payload` for structured details.

Mike Patel: How about naming conventions for enums? Lowercase snake or lower.camel? Consistency matters.

Eva Gomez: Recommend lower_snake for enum values (easier for many SIEMs). Event IDs dotted-lowercase, payload keys camelCase to match JSON consumers — but that's messy. I'd opt for consistent `snake_case` across keys and enum values to avoid confusion.

Jordan Li: Let's go `snake_case` across the board. Simpler. I'll update examples.

Jordan Li: Draft example event (cc:teams):
```json
{
  "event_id": "evt-3f9b2a",
  "schema.version": "audit.v1",
  "timestamp_iso8601": "2026-11-02T15:12:03Z",
  "event": "rbac.assignment.create",
  "actor": { "type": "user", "id": "u-914" },
  "resource": { "type": "rbac_assignment", "id": "assign-123" },
  "outcome": "success",
  "origin": "us-east-1",
  "payload": { "previous_roles": ["viewer"], "new_roles": ["editor","admin"] },
  "context": { "request_id": "req-44c", "host": "infra-12" }
}
```

Sarah Chen: That's great. Please also include `kms` example for rotation.

Jordan Li: Will do. For cross-team alignment: action items I will publish tomorrow: 1) spec doc with canonical field list + examples (rbac/kms/auth/embedding-access), 2) change log rules & schema.version policy, 3) migration plan for RBAC events when the new role API ships, 4) small compatibility tests for customers to validate event shapes.

Mike Patel: Add a checklist item for SOC/PS to review customer-facing wording & mapping. They will want sample Splunk/ELK parsers.

Eva Gomez: +1. Also add a test harness that emits sample events to a staging SIEM so teams can validate parsing and field presence.

Jordan Li: Thanks all. I'll drop the doc link here when ready and @channel ping before the sync. If anyone has immediate blockers (esp. infra or telemetry), flag them now. :thumbsup:

Sarah Chen: No blockers from infra side. We'll be ready to add `host`/`region` hooks.

Mike Patel: I'll review the draft tonight and post comments.

security-bot: Deploy note: audit-schema v1 published to staging bucket at s3://redwood-audit-specs/audit.v1.json

Jordan Li: Great — I'll circulate the staging spec and a short checklist for teams tomorrow.
